newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says U.S. has 'long way to go' on race.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says U.S. has 'long way to go' on race.

text.p: President Clinton said in remarks released Sunday that race relations remained an enduring problem in the United States.

"We've still got a long way to go before we feel truly comfortable working with each other, living with each other, relating to each other and helping solve one another's problems instead of saying, 'Well, that is their problem and not mine,'" he told Newsweek Magazine in the edition on newsstands Monday.

Clinton was to appoint an advisory panel this week to examine the state of race relations in the United States and to recommend improvements. It would be the most comprehensive study of race since President Lyndon Johnson appointed the Kerner commission after riots in Los Angeles in 1967.
In the Newsweek interview, Clinton said that white backlash would "inevitably be part of the conversation."
"(Now) you have to say to whites, 'Look, you don't have to accept blame for things that happened before you. But you do have to accept the facts of the society you live in'," he said.
Clinton said he had "a whole lot of conflicting emotions" about the criminal trial of football great O.J. Simpson, a black acquitted of killing his wife and a male friend of hers, both whites.
"After it was over, I felt that if anything good can come out of this, maybe it will be that blacks and whites and others will be more honest about how they see the world they live in," Clinton said.

After the criminal trial, Simpson was sued by the victims' survivors. The civil court jury awarded compensatory damages to the family of Ronald Goldman, Nicole Brown Simpson's friend, and $25 million in punitive damages to Goldman's parents and Nicole Simpson's estate.
